title: Ayutthaya Kingdom

endonym.native: อาณาจักรอยุธยา

capsule: The Ayutthaya Kingdom was a Tai polity founded in 1351 by King Ramathibodi I (U Thong) on an island at the confluence of the Chao Phraya, Pa Sak, and Lopburi rivers, strategically positioned to dominate regional trade between China and the Indian Ocean. At its height in the sixteenth century under King Ramathibodi II and Naresuan the Great (r.1590–1605), Ayutthaya was one of the wealthiest trading ports in Asia, attracting Chinese, Japanese, Portuguese, Dutch, and Persian merchants, and exercised suzerainty over much of mainland Southeast Asia including the Malay peninsula and parts of Cambodia. The kingdom was destroyed by the Burmese Konbaung dynasty's invasion; after a fourteen-month siege, Ayutthaya was sacked and burned in April 1767, ending 417 years of continuous rule.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Ayutthaya's core territory in the Chao Phraya basin is well attested from Dutch VOC records, royal chronicles (phongsawadan), and Portuguese accounts; tributary boundaries on the Malay peninsula and toward Cambodia are approximate and fluctuated considerably.
